summary: A 1966 timber tower on the Kootenai National Forest, successor to a 1934 tower and a 1920s cabin, retired from fire duty in the 1980s and now a popular rental.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab, 15x15 ft, on a 41-ft timber tower

access.note: Overnight rental by reservation on recreation.gov; two trails and cairned bald sections lead to the tower; high-clearance vehicle recommended for the drive. No on-site water (nearest source, Pipe Creek, is about 6 miles downhill).

visit.trail_note: Two trails descend from the lookout through forest and cairn-marked bald terrain; high-clearance vehicle recommended for road access.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Kootenai National Forest, Libby Ranger District)

events.note: First structure, a log cabin. firelookout.com gives 1928; NHLR gives 1929.
30-ft wooden tower with 7x7-ft cab added. The Western News (2016) credits the construction, and the earlier cabin, to Stef Ludvikson; NHLR and firelookout.com do not name a builder.
Current 41-ft timber tower with 15x15-ft R-6 flattop cab replaced the 1934 tower. The Western News gives 1967.
Staffed fire detection ended by the 1980s as aerial and other detection methods took over; exact year not given.
Entered the Forest Service rental program.
Accepted onto the National Historic Lookout Register, May 12, 2000 (US 341, MT 23).

corrections.proposed: Sources disagree: firelookout.com gives 1928, NHLR gives 1929, for the original log cabin.
corrections.evidence: NHLR detail page description says 'The first structure was a log cabin built in 1929'; firelookout.com's table says 'First developed in 1928 with a log cabin.'

corrections.proposed: Note the spread across sources: NHLR 5,732 ft (1,747 m), firelookout.com 5,768 ft, recreation.gov 5,780 ft. No correction to the stored value is proposed, just flagging the inconsistency for an editor.
corrections.evidence: Three sources give three different elevations for the same summit, a common artifact of old surveys vs. modern GPS.

notes_for_editor: Reasonably well documented for a rental-program lookout: two independent narrative sources (National Forest Foundation, Western News) corroborate the NHLR/firelookout.com build history. The 1980s retirement from fire duty comes from the National Forest Foundation piece; the 1984 rental start and the builder's name (Stef Ludvikson, for both the 1928 cabin and the 1934 tower) come only from the Western News article — NHLR and firelookout.com do not name a builder, so that attribution rests on a single source. Two small, unresolved conflicts flagged above: the cabin's build year (1928 vs 1929) and the summit elevation (three different figures across sources). A third, odder wrinkle: the National Forest Foundation piece implies the log cabin standing near the tower today was moved to the site in the 1950s to replace a deteriorated building, which sits awkwardly against the 1928/1929 'first structure, still there' framing from NHLR and firelookout.com — the story notes this rather than resolving it. The Purcell Mountains location also comes only from the National Forest Foundation piece. No NRHP nomination form or newspaper archive hit was found in the search budget; a Chronicling America or Montana Memory Project search might turn up more on the 1934 or 1966 construction if someone wants to dig further.
